name: Planning Data developer agreement dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 12,775 developer agreements from 78 providers; collector last ran 21 July 2026 and the dataset contains some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Use the exact authoritative agreement and linked planning application before parcel-level use; national coverage is incomplete/mixed provenance.

name: Planning Data developer agreement type dataset
fact: Planning Data defines three authoritative developer-agreement types: section-106, community-infrastructure-levy and section-278; collector last ran 19 July 2026.
gate: Agreement-type taxonomy does not prove a site has an agreement, liability or discharged obligation.

name: Section 106 developer agreement type
fact: The Planning Data model includes Section 106 as a developer-agreement type.
gate: A controlled type code is schema semantics only and is not evidence of a live S106 for a target parcel.

name: 21/00909/FUL-1 developer agreement
fact: The authoritative Isle of Wight record links developer agreement 21/00909/FUL-1 to planning application 21/00909/FUL and classifies it as section-106.
gate: Agreement existence does not prove all obligations are triggered, paid, discharged or still current.

name: SDNP/19/03210/FUL_s106 developer agreement
fact: The South Downs National Park Authority record links the S106 agreement to planning application SDNP/19/03210/FUL with start date 20 November 2019.
gate: Historic agreement linkage requires current application/permission and obligation-compliance evidence before scoring deliverability.

name: DOV/14/00842/outline-da developer agreement
fact: The Dover record links a Section 106 agreement dated 3 August 2022 to application DOV/14/00842/OUTLINE and an authority-hosted agreement document.
gate: An outline-linked S106 is not proof reserved matters, triggers, payments or implementation are complete.

name: 346-da Arun developer agreement
fact: The authoritative Arun developer-agreement record has start date 19 January 2012 and end date 16 February 2024.
gate: An end-dated agreement must not be treated as a current live obligation without newer authoritative evidence.

name: 01/02/00041-da developer agreement
fact: The Bassetlaw record links a Section 106 agreement starting 14 October 2003 to planning application 01/02/00041.
gate: Old agreement records are historical context; current title, permission and obligation status require separate verification.

name: 13/02/00001-da developer agreement
fact: The Bassetlaw record links a Section 106 agreement starting 31 July 2003 to application 13/02/00001.
gate: Age and agreement existence do not establish current enforceability, outstanding balance or development capacity.

name: 69/91/00008-da developer agreement
fact: The Bassetlaw record links a Section 106 agreement starting 18 November 1992 to application 69/91/00008.
gate: Very old agreement evidence is not current parcel readiness evidence without live register/title confirmation.

name: GOV.UK Community Infrastructure Levy guidance
fact: Updated 17 June 2026, the guidance covers charging schedules, reliefs, liability calculation, collection, spending, appeals and annual infrastructure funding statements.
gate: A published charging regime does not establish a site's final CIL liability; floorspace, permission date, relief, exemption, indexation and commencement matter.

name: GOV.UK viability guidance
fact: National viability guidance requires development contributions and viability evidence to be assessed transparently and in the relevant planning context.
gate: An applicant viability appraisal is evidence for the decision maker, not an accepted reduction in policy contributions by itself.

name: GOV.UK planning obligations guidance
fact: Planning obligations guidance covers the use, monitoring and reporting of Section 106 contributions and annual infrastructure funding statements.
gate: Authority-wide contribution reporting cannot be converted into an exact site's outstanding or discharged obligations.

name: NPPF chapter 4 decision-making
fact: NPPF paragraph 58 requires planning obligations to be necessary, directly related, and fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind; paragraph 59 sets the viability-assessment approach.
gate: Policy tests govern what may be sought; they do not prove the content or discharge state of a particular agreement.

name: London Mayoral Community Infrastructure Levy
fact: MCIL2 applies across London under the adopted schedule; the page publishes a 2026 annual rate summary and notes rates are indexed and liability depends on chargeable development and relevant reliefs/exemptions.
gate: Borough/location category and headline rate are not a final parcel liability calculation.

name: OSDC CIL charging functions decision DD2796
fact: The March 2026 GLA decision records the creation of the Oxford Street Development Corporation and anticipated transfer of planning/CIL charging functions subject to the relevant functions order and process.
gate: Charging-authority transition must be resolved by permission date and operative legal functions; do not assume the historic authority remains responsible.

name: OPDC developer contributions
fact: OPDC publishes its CIL schedule, 2026 annual rate summary and instalment policy and explains separate OPDC and Mayoral CIL processes.
gate: Rate summary and instalment policy do not establish final site liability or payment/discharge status.

name: Westminster Infrastructure Funding Statement
fact: Westminster's page, updated 24 December 2025, publishes the 2024/25 IFS covering CIL and S106 contributions and intended infrastructure funding.
gate: IFS allocation/spending is authority-level reporting and not proof a target site is mitigated, funded or deliverable.

name: Croydon CIL and Section 106
fact: Croydon publishes its latest 2024/25 annual infrastructure statement and a Section 106 approved-expenditure tracker updated through June 2026.
gate: Expenditure tracker entries and borough-wide CIL/S106 reporting do not prove a parcel's agreement, liability or infrastructure delivery.

name: Croydon CIL Charging Schedule Review
fact: Croydon's CIL review page publishes the draft charging schedule, viability study, infrastructure delivery/funding-gap evidence and 2026 examination material.
gate: A draft/review charging schedule is not the operative rate until the statutory review/adoption process is complete.

name: Cambridge Infrastructure Funding Statement
fact: Cambridge publishes an annual IFS and lists the 2024/25 statement covering contributions secured, allocated, used and retained.
gate: Reported receipts/allocations are historical authority-level finance, not a site-specific future mitigation guarantee.

name: Cambridge Community Infrastructure Levy July 2026 decision
fact: The Cambridge decision page records consultation on a draft CIL charging schedule and states CIL is intended to address strategic transport funding while S106 remains for localised infrastructure.
gate: Consultation/decision-process status must not be treated as an operative final charge for an individual development without adoption/effective-date confirmation.
